To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Tart cells are a new type of cells found in the blood of asthmatic patients, 2) they are monocytes and occasionally granulocytes with phagocytized leukocyte nuclei, 3) their incidence is increased in patients with a long time span from onset of symptoms and a high symptomatologic score, 4) they are not associated with IgE levels and are not related to antinuclear serum factors.
the prevalence of Tart cells is increased in asthmatic subjects and that the Tart cell prevalence is related to the severity of asthma and to the eosinophilia but not to the IgE.
Tart cells are a marker of the severity of the asthmatic process, that they are associated to a decrease in the serum IgE and to an increase in the symptomatology score and in the blood eosinophilia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Tart cells in the blood of asthmatic patients, and their relation to IgE and to other parameters.

the Tart cells in blood in asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of Tart cells in blood is associated with asthmatic symptoms and eosinophilia and that the absence of Tart cells is related to a higher IgE.
the presence of Tart cells is a characteristic of the asthmatic patient with a more serious form of the disease, but it is not a specific finding for asthma.
Tart cells are a new leukocyte abnormality in asthmatic blood, that they are related to the severity of the disease and that they are independent of IgE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tart cells are a new cell in the blood of asthmatic patients and that they are related to IgE and to some other parameters of the disease.
Tart cells are present in asthmatic blood in relation to IgE, sex, age, symptomatology score and blood eosinophilia.
the finding of Tart cells in the blood of asthmatic patients is a frequent phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single-cell-based method is not a good choice for the study of the disease.
Tart cells may be a useful marker of the severity of asthma and the activity of the disease.
we can use a simple, noninvasive, and cost effective approach to assess the impact of the disease on the patient's quality of life.
